items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to (allegedly) release refund
items.quote: Damit wir sie auszahlen können, überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date, 27.11.2026, as the deadline to transfer the 'Bearbeitungsgebühr'. No statutory period is involved, so the stated date is taken as given; it falls on a Friday, a normal business day, so no weekend/holiday adjustment applies. However, this entire request shows strong hallmarks of an advance-fee ('processing fee') scam, and payment is NOT recommended.

warnings: This letter shows the classic pattern of an advance-fee scam: an unsolicited, unusually large 'refund' (612,00 €) is dangled, but you are asked to pay an upfront 'processing fee' (49,90 €) before any money is released — legitimate refunds are never conditioned on paying a fee first.

The sender's address and the IBAN given for payment (CY17...) are in Cyprus, not Germany; a genuine German consumer-energy-refund body would not use a foreign shell address and a Cypriot bank account for payments from German consumers.
There is no such officially recognised German authority or ombudsman called 'Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie'; this name appears invented to sound official.

The letter uses pressure tactics (a very short, tight deadline and the threat 'Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig') typical of scam mail designed to rush victims into paying without checking.

Strong recommendation: do not transfer any money to the given IBAN; do not reply with personal/bank details; verify independently (e.g. via the Verbraucherzentrale NRW or police) and consider reporting this letter as fraud.
